originalTitle: Energy sector is in focus because of Iran, AI and California. Here are hedge funds' top plays
summary: The favorite energy stocks of hedge funds - including one with a projected 65% upside
content:
What I'm hearing from energy insiders

Greetings from Colorado, where I had the opportunity to do a nearly hour-long chat with the Chair of the Federal Trade Commission. While most of the conversation with Andrew Ferguson was about A.I. and Big Tech, we did venture a little bit into energy vis-à-vis Europe and its energy woes.

'Woes' is the correct term. The continent has been in a constant state of nervousness since the Nord Stream pipeline was blown up in 2022.

My take → It's incredible that we have satellites that can see into your car from thousands of miles high, but we still don't know who perpetrated one of the largest acts of industrial sabotage of all time.

The European energy story is one we've been reporting on at CNBC over the last 4 years. We've highlighted how critical U.S. LNG sales are to Germany and other nations, as well as the real risk of 'energy poverty' in wealthy countries like the U.K. Let's be brutally honest: Europe is not just a victim of pipeline sabotage. The continent is being hammered by a number of odd energy policy decisions, from closing zero-emission nuclear plants or shutting down natural gas facilities.

Many rational energy actors are scratching their heads. Climate risk tends to be front and center for many of these policy moves, so it's somewhat ironic that relatively mild weather the last few years has helped 'save' Europe from an even more serious energy situation.

Europe's weather luck may have run out this year, and the war in Iran is going to make things worse. Here's why.

It's been a hot summer across much of Europe. Although air conditioning is not ubiquitous across the continent - at least not yet - its use is increasing. That's raising the need to make power, which is cutting into natural gas storage levels. Europe also gets a big chunk of natural gas from shipped-in imports from the Middle East, United States and - rather ironically - Russia.

Key Point → Europe has agreed to end all imports of Russian LNG by the fall of next year, with a phase-out starting this year. It's not clear to me how you go from record imports to zero imports in twelve months, but that's the plan. Europe doing Europe things.

This data from Germany's Federal Network Agency - which tracks energy and energy storage levels - is as telling as it is a little scary. It's the "percent of storage levels" for natural gas right now. The blue line is natural gas storage from October of last year through September of this year. The orange line is the same period one year ago, with the shaded grey area a rolling average. You don't have to speak German to read this chart and see that the situation is not ideal. Natural gas storage levels are lower than last year and right at the bottom end of the rolling average. If Germany has a cold winter and power demand rises to heat homes and businesses, those storage levels will draw down quickly. If that happens, Germany will have to cut back on gas use or face increasingly low levels of gas storage heading into next year.

European demand for natural gas would seem bullish for U.S. exporters Cheniere (LNG) and Venture Global (VG) . I say 'seem' bullish because while there's no doubt Europe would like to buy our LNG, market chatter suggests many of those cargos are heading to Asia instead. Much Qatari LNG is now off-line due to Iranian attacks, and Asian buyers will be eager to snap up any excess capacity the U.S. may have.

Diesel fuel prices continue to climb higher. AAA reports the national average at $5.47 per gallon. It's higher than that in many cities around America, including the eye-watering $7 dollars per gallon in parts of California. Nationally, diesel is closing in on its nominal record high of $5.81 set back in June 2022. Piper Sandler notes that diesel and jet fuel inventories fell by a half million barrels last week when they would normally start to stay flat or even higher ahead of the fall. The Iran conflict and Russia's war on Ukraine are also contributing to higher diesel prices as a chunk of global refining capacity is now offline.

RBI → Inflation adjusted, gasoline and diesel were higher back in 2008.

Speaking of fuel costs, California historically has some of the highest fuel prices in America. Much of that is because of sky-high taxes. The state has the highest gasoline taxes in the country, adding over 70 cents for every gallon you put in the tank. Don't hold your breath hoping those ever go down. It is California, after all.

High gas prices in California aren't just because of taxes. Lack of oil refining capacity is another main reason. Already short on fuel refining, the state lost two other big refineries in the last year. Imports are needed to meet demand. Ships have been the main source of any imported fuel... but that may change in a few years if three companies get their way. If you know the state and its policies, it may seem impossible but the Golden State may get a new pipeline. The project - called Western Gateway - would come courtesy of oil, gas, pipeline and refining companies Phillips 66 (PSX) , H.F. Sinclair (DINO) and Kinder Morgan (KMI) . When built, the pipeline would connect with some already existing lines around Los Angeles and in parts of the Midwest. Here's our CNBC map of the project. It could also help neighbor Arizona, which, rather bizarrely, relies on California for much of its gasoline imports.

If you're reading this from outside the United States, you may not realize how big California and its fuel demand really are. The state is home to over 30 million registered vehicles. And while a growing number of those cars and trucks are electric, millions of Californians are driving their gasoline-powered vehicles longer distances because they are forced to live farther away from work.

chineseTitle: 由于伊朗、AI 和加州，能源行业成为焦点。以下是对冲基金的热门投资
chineseSummary: 对冲基金最喜欢的能源股 - 包括预计上涨 65% 的能源股
chineseContent:
我从能源内部人士那里听到的消息

来自科罗拉多州的问候，在那里我有机会与联邦贸易委员会主席进行了近一个小时的交谈。虽然与安德鲁·弗格森的大部分对话都是关于人工智能的。和大型科技公司，我们确实在能源领域进行了一些冒险，以应对欧洲及其能源困境。

“祸患”是正确的词。自 2022 年北溪管道爆炸以来，非洲大陆一直处于紧张状态。

我的看法 → 令人难以置信的是，我们拥有可以从数千英里高空看到你的汽车的卫星，但我们仍然不知道是谁犯下了有史以来最大的工业破坏行为之一。

过去 4 年我们一直在 CNBC 上报道欧洲能源故事。我们强调了美国液化天然气销售对德国和其他国家的重要性，以及英国等富裕国家“能源贫困”的真正风险。说实话：欧洲不仅仅是管道破坏的受害者。非洲大陆正受到一些奇怪的能源政策决定的打击，包括关闭零排放核电站或关闭天然气设施。

许多理性的能源参与者都摸不着头脑。气候风险往往是许多政策举措的首要和核心，因此具有讽刺意味的是，过去几年相对温和的天气帮助“拯救”了欧洲免遭更加严重的能源形势。

欧洲今年的天气运气可能已经耗尽，伊朗战争将使情况变得更糟。原因如下。

欧洲大部分地区正经历炎热的夏季。尽管空调在整个非洲大陆尚未普及（至少目前还没有），但其使用量正在增加。这增加了发电需求，从而削减了天然气储存水平。欧洲还从中东、美国以及俄罗斯（颇具讽刺意味的是）进口天然气中获得大量天然气。

要点 → 欧洲已同意在明年秋季之前停止进口所有俄罗斯液化天然气，并从今年开始逐步淘汰。我不清楚如何在十二个月内从创纪录的进口量变成零进口量，但这就是计划。欧洲做欧洲的事。

来自德国联邦网络局（跟踪能源和能源存储水平）的这些数据既具有说服力，又有点可怕。这是目前天然气的“存储水平百分比”。蓝线是去年10月到今年9月的天然气储存量。橙色线是一年前的同一时期，灰色阴影区域是滚动平均值。您不必说德语就能阅读此图表并发现情况并不理想。天然气储存水平低于去年，处于滚动平均值的底部。如果德国冬季寒冷，电力需求上升以供家庭和企业供暖，那么这些存储水平将迅速下降。如果发生这种情况，德国将不得不削减天然气使用量，否则明年将面临天然气储存水平日益下降的局面。

欧洲对天然气的需求似乎对美国出口商 Cheniere (LNG) 和 Venture Global (VG) 来说是乐观的。我说“似乎”看涨，因为尽管毫无疑问欧洲愿意购买我们的液化天然气，但市场传言表明其中许多货物正在运往亚洲。由于伊朗的袭击，卡塔尔的大部分液化天然气目前已停产，亚洲买家将渴望抢购美国可能拥有的过剩产能。

柴油价格继续走高。 AAA 报告全国平均价格为每加仑 5.47 美元。它比美国许多城市的价格还要高，包括加利福尼亚州部分地区每加仑 7 美元的价格。在全国范围内，柴油价格正在接近 2022 年 6 月创下的 5.81 美元的名义历史新高。派珀·桑德勒 (Piper Sandler) 指出，上周柴油和航空燃油库存减少了 50 万桶，而在下降之前通常会开始保持不变甚至更高。伊朗冲突和俄罗斯对乌克兰的战争也导致柴油价格上涨，因为全球大部分炼油产能现已停产。

印度储备银行 → 通货膨胀调整后，2008 年汽油和柴油价格较高。

说到燃油成本，加利福尼亚州历来是美国燃油价格最高的地区之一。其中很大一部分原因是高额税收。该州的汽油税是全国最高的，每加一加仑汽油就要加收 70 美分以上。不要屏住呼吸希望它们会消失。毕竟这是加利福尼亚州。

加州的高油价不仅仅是因为税收。炼油能力不足是另一个主要原因。该州本来就缺乏燃料精炼，去年还失去了另外两家大型炼油厂。需要进口来满足需求。船舶一直是所有进口燃料的主要来源……但如果三个公司如愿以偿，这种情况可能会在几年内发生变化。如果您了解该州及其政策，这似乎不可能，但金州可能会获得一条新管道。该项目名为“Western Gateway”，将由石油、天然气、管道和炼油公司 Phillips 66 (PSX)、H.F. Sinclair (DINO) 和 Kinder Morgan (KMI) 提供。建成后，该管道将与洛杉矶周边和中西部部分地区的一些现有线路连接。这是我们在 CNBC 上展示的该项目地图。它还可以帮助邻国亚利桑那州，奇怪的是，亚利桑那州的大部分汽油进口都依赖于加利福尼亚州。

如果您在美国境外阅读本文，您可能没有意识到加利福尼亚州及其燃料需求到底有多大。该州拥有超过 3000 万辆注册车辆。尽管越来越多的汽车和卡车是电动的，但数百万加州人正在驾驶汽油动力汽车行驶更远的距离，因为他们被迫居住在离工作地点更远的地方。

如果建成，西部门户可能成为一条为数百万司机降低汽油价格的管道。但是，就像加州大多数与石油或天然气相关的事情一样，在事情结束之前没有什么是确定的
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
